cards.text: Israel is getting organized to serve at the house of the LORD, and the musicians already have their assignments. Now the list turns to the men who keep watch at the doors. First up, from the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore.

cards.question: Meshelemiah's men keep watch at the doors of the house of the LORD. The list calls them the divisions of the ___

cards.text: Meshelemiah has seven sons, and then Obed-edom walks in with EIGHT. Friend, I had six little cookie cutters and I spent half my life catching them at the edge of the counter!

cards.question: Obed-edom has eight sons. What reason does the list give for it?

cards.text: Then Obed-edom's son Shemaiah has sons of his own. And those sons end up ruling over their families. Grandpa's got LEADERS in the family now.

cards.question: Why do Shemaiah's sons rule over their families?

cards.text: Shemaiah's brothers are capable men too, and Obed-edom's family adds up to 62 men with strength to do the work. Sixty-two! That's not a family, friend, that's a whole SHIFT. Meshelemiah's family brings 18 more.
Then Hosah the Merarite lists his sons, and the first name, Shimri, comes with a little note in parentheses. You know when a name gets a note, there's a story behind it.

cards.question: Shimri, the first name on Hosah's list, was Hosah's firstborn son.

cards.text: Not the firstborn, but his father appointed him first anyway, and Hosah's sons and brothers come to 13. All these gatekeeper divisions have duties ministering in the house of the LORD, just as their relatives did.

cards.question: Lots of gatekeepers, lots of gates. How do they decide who guards which gate?

answers.text: They cast lots for each gate

cards.question: When the lots are cast for the gates, who gets a turn?

cards.text: The lot for the East Gate falls to Shelemiah. Then lots are cast for his son Zechariah, and Zechariah draws the North Gate.

cards.question: Zechariah, who draws the North Gate, gets a special note in the list. It calls him a wise ___
Obed-edom draws the South Gate, and his sons draw the North Gate.

cards.text: His sons get the storehouses, and the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending highway go to Shuppim and Hosah. And there are guards at every watch, friend, which means NOBODY on this crew gets to hit snooze.

cards.question: Each day the gatekeepers spread out around the house. The biggest group, six Levites, stands on the ___ side

cards.text: The north and the south get four each, and the storehouse gets two pairs. Over on the west, there are four at the highway and two at the court. Every spot covered, every single day.

cards.question: All these gatekeeper divisions come from the descendants of which two men?

cards.text: The gates are covered. But the house of God has more than doors to look after, and now their fellow Levites get a different job.

cards.question: What are these fellow Levites put in charge of at the house of God?

cards.text: From Ladan's family, Jehieli and his sons look after the treasuries of the house of the LORD. Then comes the officer in charge of the treasuries, Shebuel, and his family tree has a BIG name in it.

cards.question: Shebuel, the officer in charge of the treasuries, is a descendant of Moses.

cards.text: Shebuel's relative Shelomith and his brothers look after the treasuries of things dedicated by King David and his commanders. Friend, I spent years guarding a takeout menu in a junk drawer. Shelomith is guarding gifts from a KING.

cards.question: Where did some of those things dedicated by David and his commanders come from?
Some of that battle plunder was dedicated to the repair of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: And these treasuries go WAY back. Even Samuel the seer, the prophet who anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13), dedicated things that are kept here.

cards.question: Which king's dedicated things are also kept in the care of Shelomith and his brothers?

cards.text: Abner son of Ner, Saul's army commander (1 Samuel 14:50), is on the list, and so is Joab son of Zeruiah, David's army commander (2 Samuel 8:16). Everything dedicated sits under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
Not every Levite here works inside the house of God. From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons get the outside duties.

cards.question: Chenaniah and his sons have outside duties as ___ and ___ over Israel

cards.text: From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives step up for all the work of the LORD and the service of the king. That's 1,700 capable men, and I used to think six cookie cutters on one counter was a CROWD.

cards.question: Hashabiah's 1,700 men are put in charge of the affairs of Israel ___ of the Jordan

cards.text: Jerijah is chief of the Hebronites. Then, in the fortieth year of David's reign, strong, capable Hebronites turn up at Jazer in Gilead.

cards.question: In the fortieth year of David's reign, how are those strong capable men at Jazer in Gilead found?

cards.text: Jerijah's relatives come to 2,700 capable men, all heads of families. King David puts them over the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

cards.question: Jerijah's 2,700 men handle the affairs of the king, but none of the matters pertaining to God.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage, that the musicians already have their assignments (1 Chronicles 25), but gives no reference for it. The card cites only 1 Chronicles 26:1.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Card 1 and the question both say these men "keep watch at the doors." That rules out "singers" and "priests" before the baker picks, so only "gatekeepers" fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Verses 2–11 are a name list with family counts. They are spread over five story cards (3, 5, 7, 8, 10) instead of being summed up in one story card.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about a detail inside the name list of verses 2–11. Obed-edom's blessing could be the standout detail on the summary card, but it can't get a choice card.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about a detail inside the name list of verses 2–11, why Shemaiah's sons rule.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The card has four sentences. It also packs in three beats: Shemaiah's brothers, Obed-edom's 62, and Meshelemiah's 18.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about a detail inside the name list of verses 2–11, whether Shimri was the firstborn.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: Shimri appointed first, Hosah's 13, and all the divisions ministering as their relatives did.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question opens with the pun "Lots of gatekeepers, lots of gates." The word "lots" points straight to the right answer, "They cast lots for each gate."

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out.

findings.problem: Verse 14 names "Shelemiah" and his son Zechariah. Cards 1 and 3 used "Meshelemiah," whose firstborn is Zechariah. The card brings in Shelemiah without saying who he is, so the baker may think he is a new man. The text never states that the two names are the same person.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin say that Shelemiah is the same man as Meshelemiah, as a clear implication of the text? Or should he leave it open, and if so, how does he meet the "New people" rule?

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording "wise counselor." Nothing earlier sets it up, so picking "counselor" over "scribe" or "builder" is luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: the sons get the storehouses, the West and Shallecheth Gates go to Shuppim and Hosah, and there are guards at every watch.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Verses 17–18 are a count of guards per post. This choice card asks for one number detail. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason that the east has the most guards, so it is luck.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Kohath and Gershon" is half arguable. Korah was a descendant of Kohath (Exodus 6:18–21), so the Korahite gatekeepers are descendants of Kohath.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question calls Saul a king, a fact from outside the passage, with no reference. Verse 28 only says "Saul son of Kish."

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "Capable Hebronites turn up at Jazer in Gilead" suggests they arrived or showed up. Verse 31 says they "were found" when the records were searched. The wording also leans toward the wrong answer "They came to the king" on card 16.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage is lists: names, counts, gate assignments and treasury posts. The long-stretch rule says a stretch gets one summary card and no choice cards, and "A stretch never gets a stop of its own." Applied strictly, the passage would have almost no choice cards.
findings.question: When an entire passage is mostly list material, which parts still count as moments that move the passage forward and can get choice cards? For example, the casting of lots, the gate assignments, the treasuries and the outside duties. And how many stops or cards should such a passage have?
